headline_marked: [[Haaland double powers Man City to victory]] over Porto in Champions League opener
headline: Haaland double powers Man City to victory over Porto in Champions League opener
summary: Erling Haaland scored twice, including a late goal, to secure a 2-0 win for Manchester City against Porto in their Champions League opener. He became City's third-highest goalscorer with 167 goals.
details: Erling Haaland scored twice, leading Manchester City to a 2-0 victory over Porto in their Champions League campaign opener. His goals secured a crucial away win for the English giants.

Haaland broke the deadlock early in the second half with a downward header after being denied by Porto goalkeeper Diogo Costa multiple times in the first half. Costa had made a hat-trick of fine saves to keep City at bay.
Porto pushed back in the second half but lacked the quality to capitalize on City's errors. Despite their efforts, they couldn't find an equalizer against Enzo Maresca's side.
Haaland sealed the win in stoppage time, clinically slotting into the bottom corner. This goal marked his 167th for City, making him the club's third-highest goalscorer of all time.

Haaland expressed satisfaction with the team's performance, stating the importance of winning on the biggest stage. He emphasized the need to win Champions League games to avoid pressure later in the season.

City's new manager Enzo Maresca, backed by significant new signings, has made a positive start. Haaland continues to be a key player, having scored five goals in his first four games of the new campaign.

headline_marked: [[Real Madrid beat Inter Milan 2-1]] in Champions League opener with Mbappe, Valverde goals
headline: Real Madrid beat Inter Milan 2-1 in Champions League opener with Mbappe, Valverde goals
summary: Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid secured a narrow 2-1 victory over his former side Inter Milan in a high-octane Champions League opener. Goals from Kylian Mbappe and Fede Valverde sealed the win.
details: Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid secured a narrow 2-1 victory over his former side Inter Milan in a high-octane Champions League opener on Tuesday. The record 15-time European champions took a two-goal lead through Kylian Mbappe and Fede Valverde.

Inter Milan's Carlos Augusto smashed home in the second half, but Cristian Chivu's team could not find an equaliser at the Santiago Bernabeu. This marked a triumphant start to the league phase for Madrid.

Madrid coach Mourinho, who led the Italian side to Champions League glory in 2010 at the same stadium, was brought back by Florentino Perez to revitalise the team. He delivered an entertaining and winning start.

Mourinho's side bounced back from a recent La Liga defeat. Goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois made several smart saves, while Inter, despite an energetic attack, was destabilised by two grievous errors at the back.
Kylian Mbappe opened the scoring in the 14th minute. Curtis Jones's poor pass put Yann Bisseck under pressure, allowing Brahim Diaz to poke the ball through to Mbappe, who swiftly fired home.
Fede Valverde netted Madrid's second goal after Inter goalkeeper Josep Martinez dallied on the ball. Valverde charged straight for him, dispossessed him, and slotted the ball into the net.
Inter's Martinez made amends for his mistake with a sensational save to thwart Jude Bellingham before half-time. Bellingham later missed another golden chance after Diaz cleverly set him up.

Courtois continued his impressive performance, pushing away Alessandro Bastoni's low drive and beating away a deflected Henrikh Mkhitaryan effort. His crucial saves ensured Madrid took all three points despite a nervy ending after Carlos Augusto's 77th-minute goal.
